title: Khmer Empire
summary: Southeast Asian state dated from 802 CE, when Jayavarman II took the title chakravartin, to 1431, when the Thai kingdom of Ayutthaya took Angkor. Angkor served as its capital for the following centuries; at its peak the empire covered much of what is now Cambodia, Thailand, Laos and southern Vietnam.

uncertainty.note: Conventional start and end dates from World History Encyclopedia; UNESCO places the Khmer capitals at Angkor between the 9th and the 15th century.

as_recorded.value: In 802 CE he took the title chakravartin

where.modern_name: Angkor, Cambodia (capital pinned: Angkor, named as capital by World History Encyclopedia; UNESCO point within the 400 km2 Angkor Archaeological Park)
where.historical_name: Angkor, capital of the Khmer Empire

importance.justification: The empire that built Angkor, whose remains UNESCO describes as the different capitals of the Khmer Empire.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List, full dataset (XML) with site coordinates

reviewer_note: Pinned at Angkor as the capital WHE names for the empire after 802; UNESCO says the park holds the remains of different capitals, so earlier capital sites are not pinned. UNESCO's point is not Angkor Wat itself (about 3 km away on the existing Angkor Wat record).
